quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: 'aroma' has no 'r' in its spelling at all. So if you hear a /r/ before 'of', where did it come from?
quests.explanation: Vowel-to-vowel transitions are smoothed out with a linking glide. Since "aroma" has no written 'r', and "of" starts with a vowel, this /r/ is purely intrusive — added by the mouth's natural movement, not by spelling.
quests.phoneticRule: In fast speech, native speakers blend and drop sounds to speak more smoothly.
